title: 2026 AMC 8 Regional Problems/Problem 22
text:
This problem involves very strategic casework, and is not easy to do.

Since none of the digits in 58 are 3, we have 3 possibilities.

1. 2 "1"s in the 10s digit, 2 "1"s in the 1s digit 2. 2 "1"s in the 10s digit, 1 "1" in the 1s digit 3. 1 "1" in the 10s digit, 2 "1"s in the 1s digit

In case 1, Let the 10s digit "1"s be in the first and second number. The third number must have tens digit 3, as it is impossible to have that many 10s come from the ones digit. Then, we have 1 case for the ones digits, being 11 31 16.

11 11 36 doesn't work because 36 does not have a 1 in it

In case 2, we must have this

1_ 1_ _1

The final 10s digit could be a 2 or a 3

Case 2.1, the final number is 31

Then, the other 2 digits must have units digits with a sum of 8, and no ones, order not mattering. This means they must be 4 4, 3 5, 2 6, or 0 8, giving 4 cases in this subcase


Case 2.2, the final number is 21

Then, the other 2 untis digits have to have a sum 18, and therefore must both be 8. So there is 1 case in this subcase.

Case 3:

In this case, we must have this

1_ _1 _1

The 2 10s digits can have sum 4 only

If the sum is 3, then the sum so far is only 42, and the final units digit cannot bring it up to 58

So, it can be 21 21 or 31 11

Then, the last digit must be 6

So there are 2 ways in case 3

Therfore, the total is 1+4+1+2 = 8 ways.

(E) 8

This took me 10 minutes to think up as a AMC8 former top 1%, very difficult for AMC8
